title: 3.7.11 Lab: `.concat()` Two Lists
description: Join two arrays into a new one with .concat(), then show both originals are unchanged. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create two arrays
steps.instructions: Create two variables, first and second, that each hold an array of at least three values.

steps.title: Join them with .concat()
steps.instructions: Use .concat() on first to join second's values onto the end, and store the result in a variable called joined.

steps.title: Print all three arrays
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print the joined array and both originals. Check that neither original changed.

requirements.title: Two arrays declared
requirements.description: Declares at least two arrays with square brackets. Help: 3.7.9 (Joining Lists with .concat())
requirements.hint: Declare two separate arrays, each in square brackets with at least three values.

requirements.title: .concat() used
requirements.hint: Call .concat on the first array and pass the second array in the parentheses.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.hint: Print the joined array and both originals so you can check that neither changed.

requirements.title: the joined list and both originals are printed
requirements.description: joined holds first followed by second, neither original was changed, and the output shows the joined array. Help: 3.7.9 (Reading: .concat())
requirements.hint: Print the joined array, then the first array, then the second, to prove the originals did not change.

checks.expr: Array.isArray(first) && Array.isArray(second) && first.length >= 3 && second.length >= 3 && JSON.stringify(joined) === JSON.stringify(first.concat(second)) && (J => joined.every(x => J.includes(String(x))))(output.join(' '))
checks.fail: joined should be first followed by second (and neither original changed), and your output should show it.
